newsitem.title: TAIWAN: In Taiwan stocks, hi-tech selloff buries HK relief.
newsitem.headline: In Taiwan stocks, hi-tech selloff buries HK relief.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mildly lower on Wednesday as heavy profit-taking in electronics negated solid advances in most other sectors in the first session since arch rival Beijing took over Hong Kong, brokers said.

The market had stamped its approval on Hong Kong's shift to communist sovereignty by opening higher and jumping as high as 9,124.30 in early trade. But late selling on electronics dropped the index by 33.56 points or 0.37 percent at close to 8,996.72.
Turnover was a very heavy at T$182 billion.
High-tech shares, whose recent bull run had helped the index gain more than 10 percent in June, plunged 5.44 percent.

"The Hong Kong handover turned into a positive factor for the market because nothing negative came out of it, and the handover process so far has been smooth," said Lin Long-hsien, senior analyst for United Securities.
Yungli analyst Chen Han-chung said the overall market was spared a plunge because funds taken out of electronics were re-invested into other sectors.
"Electronics simply did not have enough technical room to keep on supporting the market," Chen said.
The heavily weighted financials, seen as having lagged in the market's June bull run, gained 1.39 percent.
Construction shares, boosted by hopes of a continued economic recovery, soared 4.24 percent.
But it was widespread declines in Taiwan's closely watched computer microchip makers that handcuffed the market.

Taiwan's top chipmaker, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, plunged the daily seven-percent limit or T$8.50 to finish at T$115. The second largest, United Microelectronics, also closed limit-down, losing T$7.50 to T$106.
Brokers said they expected the overall index to settle into a consolidation while investors continued to transfer funds from electronics into cheaper shares.
